title: Tasks
description: One project's tasks: epics hold features, a feature's plan holds tickets, a ticket holds subtickets. An item is approved when the user approved it or, with children, when all of them are. An item can't be built before the items in its `blockedBy`, nor before those of its parents, are done; it can be approved anyway, and then waits. The user may also cancel an item (it won't be built), leave notes on it, and answer a feature's open questions, all in the viewer. Ids never change: a new feature or ticket takes the next number under its parent (TK-3.2 is TK-3's second ticket, TK-3.2.1 that ticket's first subticket). Every title says what is done, verb first: Add, Update, Replace, Move, Split, Merge, Delete, or Fix <what goes wrong> when <it happens>. Text is markdown: `code`, **bold**, links; an id (TK-3, GW-13.2) links to its page in the viewer. A feature's or a ticket's `description` may also hold paragraphs (a blank line between), `- ` lists and ``` fenced code: the interfaces and types a ticket defines.

repo.description: The repository these tasks belong to.

prefix.description: The id prefix of every feature and ticket in this file: TK (tickets), GW (gateway), BH (bh), IC (items-core), AU (auth), IA (items-app).

intro.description: What this list is, and notes that hold for all of it.

repo.description: A repository (`../<name>`); "live gateway" is the running gateway on this machine (its bh page, its stored stacks, its deploys); "gcp" is Google Cloud and its consoles. bh's packages are copied into the apps after a release, never edited under their `packages/bh/`.

title.description: What is done, verb first: "Add submenus to `Menu`", "Fix duplicate option ids when two `Select`s share a page".

description.description: What it is, in a sentence or two.

status.description: Not planned: written down only. Planning: being planned now. Planned: a plan, ready to build. Designed: a design exists (a feature with a `design` and a plan stays Planned). In progress. Done.

waitingOn.description: What it waits for that isn't an item, in words: "your choices (below)". Items it waits for go in `blockedBy`.

statusNote.description: A word on the status: the commit it landed in, what's left.

approved.description: The user approved it. Kept only on an item with no children: a feature with a plan, a ticket with subtickets and every epic are approved when all their children are, which is worked out, never stored. The viewer's Approve sets it (approving a parent sets every item under it).

today.description: What's there today, with paths and counts.

stays.description: What it leaves as it is, and why.

chosen.description: What's decided; "your answer" marks the user's own decisions.

openChoices.description: Questions the user answers, each with its options. The viewer shows them under the feature, where the user picks an option or writes their own (`answer`). A session folds an answered one into `chosen` and the plan, then removes it; it never answers one itself.

design.description: The design: a link and what it adds.

plan.description: The tickets, in order. None while it is not planned.

approved.description: The user approved it. Kept only on an item with no children: a feature with a plan, a ticket with subtickets and every epic are approved when all their children are, which is worked out, never stored. The viewer's Approve sets it (approving a parent sets every item under it).

byYou.description: The user does it: console access, an external account, credentials, a go/no-go.

blockedBy.description: What must be done first. Its children wait on these too, so they aren't repeated below it. Name the most specific item (a ticket, not its feature, when only the ticket is needed); never the item's own parent or child; no cycles.

id.description: A feature or ticket (TK-2.2, GW-13), or an epic as prefix/id (TK/E4), in any file.

why.description: What it needs from it, in a few words: "uses `Select`'s option groups".

cancelled.description: The user cancelled it: it won't be built. Kept only on an item with no children, like `approved`, and never beside it; a parent is cancelled when all its children are. The viewer's Cancel sets it (cancelling a parent cancels every item under it).

notes.description: Words on it, oldest first, written in the viewer: the user's, and the planner session's replies (`by: "claude"`). A session reads the user's as their words about the item.

at.description: When it was written, in UTC; also the note's key.

by.description: Who wrote it, when it isn't the user: `claude` is the planner session, replying.

quote.description: The fragment of the item's description the note is about, as the user selected it (whitespace collapsed). A reply about the same fragment carries the same quote.

nth.description: Which place of the quote it is, from 0, when the description has it more than once.

seen.description: On the user's notes: when the planner took it in (replied, acted on it, or just read it). A note without it is still to be read.

closed.description: When the user closed its thread (the item's own notes, or one quoted fragment's). A thread is closed while all its notes are; the viewer shows it as one line.

question.description: The question, whole: it names its subject, so it reads on its own.

options.description: The answers to pick from, each whole.

recommended.description: The index in `options` of the recommended answer.

notes.description: The talk about the question: an answer of the user's that asked something instead (moved here when the planner replied), and the planner's replies.

answer.description: The user's answer: one of the options as written, or their own words. A session folds it into `chosen` and the plan, or, when it asks something, moves it into `notes` with a reply.

part.description: The part of the repository: a package, an app, a path.

block.description: Text: a paragraph, a list, or a paragraph with a list under it.

item.description: A list item: its text, or its text with a list under it.
